verdict.rationale: Skyfire's Know Your Agent (KYA) system ships signed JWT credentials that package agent identity. It offers optional Individual or Organization verification tiers that attach real-world identity. Sellers can set identity requirements per service, and token creation fails when a buyer is not verified to the required level. The docs also say bot managers can identify the agent or agent platform and let it through, so merchants can tell trusted agent traffic from anonymous bots. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that merchants can verify token signatures and distinguish verification tiers in practice.

support.subject: As a merchant, agents identify themselves verifiably — registered profiles, signatures, or trust tiers — so I can tell trusted agent traffic from anonymous bots

citations.quote: A KYAPay token is a signed, interoperable credential that packages agent identity and payment intent into a verifiable envelope.
If a buyer is not verified to the level a service requires, token creation fails and the transaction does not proceed.
The site, or the bot manager in front of it, can then identify the agent/agent platform and allow it through rather than block it.
From the merchant's side, an agentic purchase is never anonymous.
Verified buyers can use a broader set of seller services, including those that require trusted credentials.
